entries.meaning: ‘Brother, no dharma equals benefiting others and no baseness equals causing others pain. This is the settled verdict of all Puranas and Vedas; the wise know it, dear one. Those who take human bodies and hurt others must suffer the terrible fear of repeated existence. Deluded people commit many sins, absorbed in self-interest and destroying their own hereafter. To them, brother, I am Time embodied, giving the fruit of good and evil deeds. The truly wise reflect in this way and worship me, knowing the sorrow of transmigration. They relinquish actions that bear good or evil fruit and worship me, Lord of gods, humans and sages. I have described the qualities of saints and non-saints; those who keep them in view do not fall into worldly existence.’

Hearing the words from the Lord's own mouth, all the brothers rejoiced; love could not be contained in their hearts. Again and again they made humble petitions, while Hanuman's heart overflowed with joy. Raghupati then returned to his own palace, daily performing ever-new deeds in this way. Sage Narada came repeatedly and sang Rama's purifying deeds. Each day he beheld those ever-fresh feet, then went to Brahma's realm and recounted the whole story. Hearing it, Brahma felt the highest joy and said again and again, ‘Dear son, sing his virtues.’ Sanaka and his companions praised Narada. Though those sages were absorbed in Brahman, hearing the song of Rama's virtues they left samadhi behind and listened reverently, supremely fit recipients that they were.

Once Raghunatha summoned everyone: his teacher, Brahmins and city-dwellers all came. When the teacher, sages, Brahmins and good people were seated, the Lord—who breaks his devotees' worldly bondage—said: ‘All citizens, hear my words. I speak with no possessive attachment in my heart. There is neither injustice nor a show of authority in this: listen and do whatever seems right to you. That person alone is my servant and dearest to me who accepts my direction. But, brothers, if I speak anything unjust, stop me without fear. By great fortune you have obtained a human body, which all scriptures call rare even for gods: the abode of spiritual practice and gateway to liberation. Whoever gains it yet fails to prepare the life beyond…’

‘The fruit of this body, brother, is not sensual enjoyment; even heaven is brief and ends in sorrow. Fools who obtain a human body but set their minds on pleasure trade nectar back for poison. No one ever calls a person good who loses the philosopher's stone and picks up a seed-bead. The imperishable soul wanders among 8.4 million forms in four modes of birth, forever driven by Maya and enclosed by time, karma, nature and qualities. Sometimes, through causeless compassion, the loving Lord gives it a human body. The human body is a vessel for the ocean of becoming; my grace is the favourable wind, a true teacher its helmsman, and the vessel a sturdy boat. Thus one has readily obtained equipment that is otherwise rare.’

‘If you desire happiness here and beyond, listen and hold my words firmly in your heart. Brother, this path is accessible and joyful: devotion to me, praised by Purana and revelation. Knowledge is difficult of access and beset by obstacles; its discipline is hard, and the mind has no support in it. A person may endure much hardship and attain it, yet one without devotion is not dear to me. Devotion is independent, a mine of every joy, but living beings do not gain it without holy company. Saints are not met without a mass of merit; holy company ends transmigration. In the world there is one unrivalled meritorious act: worshipping Brahmins' feet in thought, deed and speech. Sages and gods favour the person who abandons deceit and serves a Brahmin.’

‘Tell me, what exertion does devotion's path require? No yoga, sacrifice, repetition, austerity or fasting—only a straightforward nature, no crookedness of mind, and constant contentment with whatever comes. If a person calls himself my servant but puts hope in people, tell me, what trust has he in me? Why say much and prolong the account? Brother, conduct of this kind brings me under one's sway: no enmity or quarrel, no expectation or fear; for such a person every direction is always full of joy. Undertaking no possessive projects, without a fixed home, unassuming, sinless, free of anger, skilful and discerning; always loving the company of the good and regarding sense-pleasure, heaven and liberation as straw; firm in devotion's cause but free of folly, and sweeping every perverse argument far away.’

Hearing Rama's nectar-like words, everyone clasped the feet of the abode of grace: ‘You are our mother, father, teacher and kinsman, treasure of compassion and dearer than life. Body, wealth and home are beneficial only for Rama; in every way you remove the suffering of those who bow to you. None but you gives such instruction—even mother and father remain concerned with their own interest. In every age only you and your servants, enemy of demons, help the world without motive. All friendship in the world serves self-interest; even in dreams, Lord, there is no ultimate good apart from you.’ Hearing everyone's words steeped in the flavour of love, Raghunatha rejoiced in his heart. With his permission they returned to their several homes, describing the Lord's delightful conversation.

Once sage Vasishtha came to Rama, the lovely abode of bliss. Raghunayaka received him with the highest honour, washed his feet and took the water from them. The sage joined his hands: ‘Rama, listen; ocean of grace, I have a request. The more I behold your conduct, the more boundless my bewilderment becomes. The Vedas do not know your immeasurable majesty—how then can I describe it, Lord? The work of a family priest is very lowly; Veda, Purana and Smriti condemn it. When I was unwilling to accept it, Brahma told me of its eventual gain: “The Supreme Self, Brahman in human form, will become a king and ornament of Raghu's line.”’

‘Repetition, austerity, vows, yoga, one's own dharma, the many good rites born of revelation; knowledge, compassion, self-restraint and bathing at holy places—every dharma praised by revelation and the good; the many Agamas, Vedas and Puranas, whether read or heard: Lord, their one fruit is constant love for your lotus feet. This is the lovely fruit of every discipline. Can filth be removed by washing it with filth? Can anyone obtain clarified butter by churning water? Raghuraya, without the water of loving devotion, inward impurity never departs. That person alone is all-knowing, a knower of truth and learned; that person alone is an abode of virtues with unbroken realization, capable and endowed with every excellent mark, in whose heart there is love for your lotus feet.’

Having spoken thus, sage Vasishtha returned home, deeply pleasing the ocean of grace. The giver of joy then took Hanuman, Bharata and the other brothers and attendants outside the city, where he had elephants, chariots and horses summoned. Rama graciously looked upon them all and praised them, giving the appropriate ones to whoever wanted them. Weariness's remover took on weariness himself and went to a cool mango grove. Bharata spread out his own garment; the Lord sat, and all the brothers served him. Hanuman began to fan him, body thrilled and eyes filling with tears. None is as fortunate as Hanuman, none so attached to Rama's feet. O Girija, the Lord has repeatedly praised with his own mouth Hanuman's loving service.
